details: Fireline is a historical fire-activity exploration project for Punjab, India. It uses NASA FIRMS active-fire observations from two satellite products: MODIS Terra Standard Processing and VIIRS Suomi-NPP Standard Processing. The project brings these observations into a shared geographic and temporal framework so users can explore where and when satellite-detected fire activity was recorded. The data workflow prepares observations for analysis by checking and standardizing fields, clipping records to Punjab, and assigning detections to spatial grid cells. It aggregates activity by week and calendar month at Punjab-wide, grid-cell, and district levels. The processed measures include detection counts, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), day and night detections, and the number of active cells. The original sensor identity and measurements are retained throughout the workflow. Fireline’s harmonization approach supports comparison through consistent spatial and time groupings and sensor-specific historical percentiles. This allows users to explore each sensor’s activity in the context of its own historical record. The resulting datasets support maps, time-series charts, calendar views, district comparisons, and anomaly exploration. The project backend is built with FastAPI and DuckDB, with processed data stored in Parquet format. Its API provides data for historical series, calendars, districts, hotspots, anomalies, map views, and exports. Fireline is designed to help people explore historical patterns and periods of elevated satellite-detected activity in Punjab.
